text:
kenji: FYI since ~09:04 UTC we're seeing burst ECC corrections + fan-controller resets on four GPUs in rack r12 (gpu-node-82,83,84,85). Nodes have had soft reboots; telemetry shows temps spiking to ~92C then RPMs dropping. tagging eng-infra.

maya: Can you paste the recent dmesg + BMC/ipmitool outputs? Need to know if this is thermal, power, or MCU/firmware.

kenji: dmesg snippet pasted to ticket:
---
[09:05] NVRM: Xid (0001:68): GPU 1: ECC corrected errors
[09:06] kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU fan controller timeout
[09:07] kernel: watchdog: GPU reset failed, scheduling node reboot
---
Also attached ipmitool sensor for gpu-node-83: fans spike then briefly report 0 RPM.

sam_ops: Recommend preemptive drains on 82/83 and reprovision spares before touching 84/85. If autoscaler can't satisfy capacity, shift non-critical routes to eu-west fallback earlier to avoid customer SLO impact.

lisa: Impact calc: these are in Dedicated-ml-large. Losing 4 blades -> ~20% throughput drop at p95 for that pool. If autoscaler spins same-AZ spares we might still be constrained. Estimated cost for two temporary spares + routing = ~$1.2k/day. Approve if it prevents SLA breaches.

infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-2026-2043 \u2014 "r12 GPU fan-controller + ECC burst". Priority: P2. Assigned: @oncall.

oncall: Acknowledged. I'll coordinate. Starting staggered cordon+drain on gpu-node-82 then 83 to avoid a big hole. ETA 10-15m.

jorge: Vendor (Supermicro) confirms a firmware MCU bug affecting a subset of boards; RMA lead time 3-5 business days unless we escalate. We have two spare blades in rack r14 we can provision as temp replacements.

maya: Also seeing repeated PCIe AER entries for gpu-node-84 in the kernel logs. Can infra check chassis voltages/fans via BMC? Please collect BMC SEL as well.

kenji: Attached ipmitool logs in the ticket. gpu-node-83 shows intermittent fan controller resets correlated with ECC spikes.

sam_ops: Drain commands for reference (run cordon first):
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-82
kubectl drain gpu-node-82 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
Annotate latency-sensitive services (annotation: "latency-sensitive=true") so we don't evict critical frontends.

oncall: Update: gpu-node-82 and 83 drained successfully and pods rescheduled. Two long-running local-storage jobs blocked on eviction; owners notified. Holding off on 84/85 drain until spares join.

jorge: Spares provisioning in r14 in progress; will label them `dedicated:ml-large,temp-spare=yes`. ETA ~18m for k8s join.

lisa: Confirmed autoscaler quotas in region are borderline but adequate for this short window. Watch the batch job at ~11:30UTC which could exhaust spare capacity.

sam_ops: Once spares join, we'll migrate non-enterprise routes to eu-west if pool throughput < 85% of SLO. Also recommend adding a fan-controller health alert and a firmware-check step in reprovision runbook.

maya: I'll collect kernel oops, BMC SEL, and aggregate ECC telemetry. Will push a blameless incident summary + RMA timeline once vendor responds. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INF-2026-2043 updated: status=mitigating, temp_spares=2.

oncall: Pool is back to ~95% after spares joined and rescheduling. Monitoring p95 latency and ECC telemetry closely. Closing here unless we see new reboots; escalate to P1 if nodes start hard-rebooting.

kenji: Thanks all. If anyone sees fresh AER or fan resets, ping this thread and tag @oncall and @jorge.
